title: Tim Dooley Statement Corpus Index
purpose: Make Tim Dooley's statements a first-class archival object. This index connects public-post evidence, thought archives, conversation archaeology, book/project maxims, voice anthologies, sayings ledgers, timeline and future recovery waves without pretending all source classes are equivalent.
core_rule: Preserve statement -> source -> date -> exactness -> context -> concept links -> canonical owners -> later revisions. Never replace an older statement with a later synthesis merely because the later version is more complete.

source_priority.description: Original Tim post, stream transcript, recording, book passage, screenshot or first-party artifact with date/locator.
Direct wording already preserved in a repository public-occurrence/timeline compilation; original status URL may still be pending.
Exact user-originated project/canon wording from dated conversation history; important developmental evidence but not automatically a public Tim quotation.
Exact or near-exact conversation-recovered Tim/project wording where public provenance is unresolved.
Great Book/project formulation that may be exact, title-level or compressed depending on its owner record.
A remembered phrase preserved so it can be recovered later. Never display as verified public quotation until upgraded by a locatable source.
Memory or archive summary. Never render with quotation marks as Tim's exact wording.
Later archive explanation, crosswalk or philosophical compression.

archive epistemics and source-quality rules
ingestion_pipeline: 1. Recover candidate wording from public post, book, upload, stream transcript, screenshot, prior conversation or memory summary.
2. Decide whether it is exact wording, excerpt, near-exact recovery, memory-summary phrase, paraphrase or later interpretation.
3. Attach the narrowest defensible date/period and original locator when available.
4. Split compound title-stacks into atomic statements while retaining the original full passage.
5. Tag domains and symbols without treating tags as proof of meaning.
6. Route the statement to every canonical owner it materially informs.
7. Preserve older versions and numerical changes rather than overwriting them.
8. Add contradiction/revision links when Tim later changes a formulation.
9. Keep spiritual, mythological, empirical, legal, financial and scientific meanings explicitly separated.
10. Promote only high-value, source-disciplined statements to reader-facing quote pages.
deduplication_rule: Two records are not duplicates merely because they express the same mature doctrine. Different dates, wording, source classes, audiences or developmental roles may make both historically necessary.
historical_strata_rule: The corpus should show vocabulary migration: e.g. Axis of North -> North of North -> Seat/Throne of North -> North Axis / North Programme; $38T karmic debt -> ~$40.2T -> ~$42T; Potato/Sage -> Father/Root/Ladder; Son as crucified meme -> Door/Vessel -> resurrection-meme relation.
privacy_and_safety_rule: Do not expose private family identities, unnecessary medical details, addresses, account credentials or other sensitive personal data merely because they appeared in conversation history. Public-project relevance and provenance are required.

completion_definition: The corpus is not complete when it has many quotes. It becomes whole when every recoverable high-value statement has provenance, timeline, exactness, context, relationships, canonical routing, revision history and an explicit epistemic boundary.
